notes: Perfect claim overlap (C32-C36, C111-C113) regarding reduced average activity for trained sequences. LLM finds evidence well-supported with appropriate corrections, while peer reviewers express uncertainty, requesting direct statistical comparisons between trained and untrained conditions rather than accepting indirect comparisons.

High overlap (C48-C50, C86, C95-C97) on dimensionality analysis showing sequences encoded in unique spatial patterns requiring multiple components. Both evaluations accept the sophisticated analytical approach and its conclusions without challenge.

Strong overlap (C42-C46) on temporal analysis and instruction/execution phase confounding. Both identify the same limitation: inability to separate instruction-related from execution-related activity patterns. Both request additional analyses to clarify contributions of each phase.

Strong overlap (C38-C39, C75, C81-C82, C84-C85) on MVPA findings in IPS and parietal regions. Both accept that robust sequence discrimination occurs in these areas. Peer reviewers describe findings as 'exciting' and 'novel,' requesting expanded discussion rather than questioning validity.

Strong overlap (C22-C25, C27-C31) on behavioral findings of sequence-specific and general learning. Both accept the statistical evidence for learning effects. Peer reviewers request better presentation in Abstract/figures but affirm the results themselves.

Moderate overlap (C6, C51-C55, C93-C94) on core finding that trained sequences show higher classification accuracy than untrained. Both accept this central result. Peer reviewers praise it as 'elegant' and 'novel,' while LLM notes multiple converging analyses support the finding.

Partial overlap (C64-C65) on pattern decomposition showing common component explains 99% of variance with <1% sequence-specific. Both accept this finding. Peer reviewers request it be emphasized more prominently and ask about behavioral correlations, indicating interest in extending rather than challenging the result.

Minimal overlap (C88) on phonological rehearsal as alternative explanation. Both express uncertainty about whether observed patterns reflect motor sequences or subvocal rehearsal strategies. LLM notes multiple alternative explanations remain speculative; peer reviewers specifically raise pre-SMA word repetition concern.

Overlap on control analyses (C60-C62) showing classification accuracy differences not due to behavioral confounds. Peer reviewers implicitly accept these controls by not challenging them despite scrutinizing other methodological aspects. LLM explicitly notes effect survives correction for behavioral differences.

Claims C108-C110 on bilateral/left-lateralized learning effects and intermanual transfer appear only in LLM results. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific claims about hemispheric lateralization.

Claims C114-C122 on synthesis of competing mechanisms (recruitment vs. efficiency) and how MVPA reveals specialization despite complex average activity changes appear only in LLM results. No corresponding peer review evaluation of this theoretical framework.

Claims C69-C74, C87, C89-C90, C92 on mechanistic interpretation of sequentially-tuned neurons and spatial resolution requirements appear primarily in LLM results. LLM appropriately marks as speculative. Peer review R7 touches on related concerns (C88) but doesn't evaluate the full mechanistic framework.

Claims C123-C132 on methodological description quality and Figure 1 details appear only in peer review. These are presentation/clarity concerns rather than substantive scientific claims. LLM results include some overlapping claims (C18-C19) but don't evaluate methodological description adequacy.

Minimal overlap (C5, C66) on basic MVPA capability to discriminate sequences. Both accept that classification works in multiple regions. This represents agreement on foundational methodology underlying more specific findings evaluated in other result pairs.

Minimal overlap (C63) on sequence-specific component following training. Both accept this finding as part of broader pattern decomposition results. Agreement on this specific aspect of the more comprehensive analyses evaluated in other pairings.
